func_802155F4_6745A4.title: Dungeon map floor-panel constructor
func_802155F4_6745A4.summary: Creates the dungeon pause-map floor panel, floor labels and the local character head.
behavior: The file_17 constructor creates a child task whose update callback is func_80215198_674148 and finalizer is func_80215474_674424. Allocation failure returns null after cleanup.
The character, dungeon index and actual floor are stack arguments at entry offsets 0x1C, 0x20 and 0x24. Arguments at 0x10 through 0x18 are unused by the inspected implementation.
Task words +0x90, +0x94 and +0x98 hold dungeon index, selected floor and floor count. The selected floor can change independently of the local character head.
The local head is a kind-2 display record using model 0x48000040 + character*0xE0, animation 0xA0216AE0, file 0x04D1, scale 3.0 and rotation sentinels 0x8000. Its layer is the panel layer plus two.

The head uses relative screen X 53 and Y 53 + (112/(floor_count+1))*(floor_count-floor). Integer division occurs before multiplication. func_800115E0_121E0 writes the relative position into the record at +0x80/+0x84.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.
Keep display records owned by this task so native cleanup can reclaim them. Do not retain their pointers across panel creation.
func_802155F4_6745A4.declaration: extern void *func_802155F4_6745A4(void *owner, int x, int y, int layer, unsigned int unused4, unsigned int unused5, unsigned int unused6, int character, int dungeon, int floor);

func_80215198_674148.title: Dungeon floor-panel update
func_80215198_674148.summary: Updates the dungeon map floor panel and resolves its relative display positions.
behavior: This file_17 callback belongs to the task created by func_802155F4_6745A4. The callback resolves parent-relative positions with func_8001136C_11F6C before drawing the panel.
Task +0x90 is the dungeon index, +0x94 the selected floor and +0x98 the floor count, all 32-bit words. +0x6C/+0x70 are the resolved screen origin.
The floor rows use func_80215150_674100. Existing display-object links and cached panel buffers must remain intact.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.

func_80215150_674100.title: Dungeon floor-row spacing
func_80215150_674100.summary: Calculates a dungeon floor row Y coordinate using native integer spacing.
behavior: Returns 37 + (112/(floor_count+1))*ordinal, with integer division. The top row has ordinal one.
For a zero-based gameplay floor, ordinal is floor_count-floor. The native character head adds 16 to this return value.
The five dungeon definitions contain 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2 floors, respectively.
cautions: The function belongs to file_17. A floor_count of -1 divides by zero.
func_80215150_674100.declaration: extern int func_80215150_674100(int ordinal, int floor_count);

func_80215CA4_5D1174.title: Room minimap update and lifecycle
func_80215CA4_5D1174.summary: Initializes, opens and fades the native in-game room minimap.
behavior: The file_0D callback uses task +0xDC as a 32-bit state: zero initializes, one is hidden, two is open and three fades out.
Initialization reads origin X/Y from object floats +0x08/+0x0C and world extent from object u16 +0x14. These become system +0x3B000/+0x3B004/+0x3B008. Room 0x0132 overrides extent with 6900.

Initialization releases the task's old display records and appends compass, local marker and map background as kind-1 records. Task +0xE0 points to the local marker, +0xE8 to the compass; +0xE4 is a 32-bit shape selector (zero rectangular, nonzero square).
In states two and three it calls func_80216228_5D16F8 for the local marker. It obtains the map background by following the first link of that marker, so inserting between them breaks native fading.
The map background and compass fade between alpha zero and 160. The local marker blinks independently. Sprite alpha is byte +0x10; screen coordinates are signed shorts +0x1C/+0x20.
All attached records belong to the native task. Additional records may be appended after the background without changing the local-to-background link.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.
State zero may invalidate every previously retained display pointer. An allocation failure can destroy the task before initialization finishes.

func_80216228_5D16F8.title: Minimap local-marker projection
func_80216228_5D16F8.summary: Projects the local player into the room minimap and updates its blinking directional marker.
behavior: The scale is 128.0 divided by unsigned system word +0x3B008. World X/Z are read from the local player display record.
For system u16 orientation +0xCF88E equal to 0, 0x100 and 0x200, projected axes are (-X,-Z), (Z,-X) and (X,Z), respectively. The remaining branch uses (-Z,X). Multiply both axes by the scale.
Truncate each scaled offset toward zero, add the corresponding origin at system +0x3B000/+0x3B004 and add 13. Clamp X to 8..144. Clamp Y to 8..80 for task +0xE4 equal to zero, otherwise 8..144.

The function also changes task +0xD8 and sprite alpha for the local blink, and selects one of sixteen direction descriptors according to orientation and local heading. It is not a pure coordinate helper.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.
Calling this routine for another player still reads the local player and mutates the local blink state. Use its verified projection formula for independent markers.

func_801FB2D0_5B71E0.title: Height-dependent dungeon floor update
func_801FB2D0_5B71E0.summary: Resolves floors in vertical dungeon rooms and updates native exploration state.
behavior: The file_0C updater switches on the room's special-floor rule. Its vertical comparisons are strict greater-than tests against local world Y.
Rules 1..9 respectively use thresholds -150, -80, 130, 120, 305, 392, (-115 and -372), -120, and 100. Rule seven selects floor two above -115, floor one above -372, otherwise floor zero.
Other branches also distinguish subrooms using X or Z and update visited-room flags. Replaying this routine to locate another player would alter local exploration state.
cautions: This is an observation hook, not a recovered callable prototype. For read-only floor classification, use the decoded room and height rules without invoking the updater.

D_80209B9C_5C5AAC.title: Dungeon room-to-floor table pointers
D_80209B9C_5C5AAC.summary: Five file_0C pointers select native room, floor and vertical-rule tables.
behavior: Each table contains three-byte records: raw room ID, zero-based floor and special vertical-rule ID. A room byte of 0xFF ends the table.

Some rooms appear more than once because they span floors. Native lookup starts with the first matching record; the height updater then resolves the actual floor. There are 116 distinct dungeon/room pairs.
The initial table pointers are 0x80209A00, 0x80209A50, 0x80209AA4, 0x80209AF4 and 0x80209B48. These are overlay data, not save-state pointers.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.
This example reads only the first matching floor. Apply its special height rule for rooms spanning floors.

D_80209BC8.title: Minimap position-dot sprite descriptor
D_80209BC8.summary: Native 12-byte descriptor selecting the 8 by 8 position dot from resource 0x8004.
behavior: The descriptor is six big-endian halfwords: C003, 0808, 0000, 0000, 0300, 0300. C003 loads texture-bank entry three and ends the sprite command sequence.
The dimensions are 8 by 8. Texture coordinates are stored in thirty-seconds of a pixel; 0x0300 selects X=24, Y=24 in the 64 by 32 sheet.
D_80209CA0 entry three refers to loaded file 0x007F and segmented address 0x0A000000. Its original pixels come from PIC resource 0x8004, not from the descriptor itself.
The minimap constructor initially selects this round red dot. Open-map updates select directional descriptors from the same native texture system.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.

D_80209CA0.title: Minimap native texture bank
D_80209CA0.summary: Six 16-byte texture descriptors supply the room minimap, compass and local marker.
behavior: Each entry stores u16 width at +0, u16 height at +2, format byte at +4, texture address at +8 and file ID at +0x0C.
Entry three is a 64 by 32 RGBA5551 sheet: format 0x10, segmented address 0x0A000000 and file 0x007F. It supplies the round position dot and some directional markers.
Entries four and five use the same dimensions and file, at 0x0A00B000 and 0x0A00D000. Their resources are 0x800F and 0x8011. Entries one and two are modified when a room map is initialized.
File zero means a direct texture pointer. A nonzero file requires the file's loaded base and segment mapping; do not interpret a segmented address as a CPU pointer.
cautions: Only access this layout while its owning overlay and task are active. Task-pool addresses can be reused after destruction.
The table stores texture descriptors, not the opaque texture handles used by the pause-menu image system.

D_800657CC_663CC.title: HUD file resource-to-segment list
D_800657CC_663CC.summary: Pairs of resource IDs and destination addresses populate native loaded file 0x007F.
behavior: This list maps image resources 0x8004 through 0x8019 to decoded 0x1000-byte slots beginning at segmented address 0x0A000000.
The first pair is (0x8004, 0x0A000000), resource 0x800F maps to 0x0A00B000 and 0x8011 maps to 0x0A00D000. A zero resource ID ends the list.

The native resource loader decodes each PIC image into the loaded file's destination. File 0x007F therefore refers to the populated runtime allocation, not a single packed texture at the same file-table index.
